name: Zaboud
overview: Zaboud is a male biblical figure identified as the son of Hammuel and the father of Zaccur, mentioned specifically in 1 Chronicles 4:26. His tribal affiliation is not recorded in the biblical text. Notably, the name Zaboud does not appear in the Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia (BHS) Hebrew text but is preserved in the Rahlfs Septuagint, indicating a textual variation in ancient manuscripts.
namesAndTitles: The name Zaboud appears only once in Scripture, in 1 Chronicles 4:26, without any explicit meaning provided in the biblical text or the Septuagint. Therefore, Zaboud is simply recognized as a proper name without additional semantic or theological significance noted.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Zaboud's family connections as the son of Hammuel and the father of Zaccur. Beyond these relationships, no further family ties or relational details are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Zaboud's mention in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles serves to preserve the lineage and heritage of certain families in Israel, emphasizing the continuity of God's people. The textual presence of his name in the Septuagint but absence in the Hebrew text highlights the complexities of biblical transmission and the importance of careful textual study. Although Zaboud himself does not play a prominent role in biblical narratives, his inclusion contributes to the broader biblical emphasis on ancestry and God's providential care in preserving His covenant community.
